title: Walls And Gates
statement: You get a grid of rooms. -1 is a wall, 0 is a gate, and 2147483647 (call it INF) is an empty room. You can move up, down, left or right, never through a wall. Give each empty room the number of steps to its nearest gate. A room that no gate can reach stays INF.

example.caption: Two gates in opposite corners. Each room takes the distance to whichever gate is closer. The wall stays -1.

idea.sentence: Start from all the gates at once and spread outward one ring at a time. The first time a ring reaches a room is its shortest distance, so write the ring number there.

jargon.plain: Breadth-first search that starts from many cells at once. All starts are at distance 0, and each ring is one step further out.
A big number that stands for 'not reached yet'. Here 2147483647. A room that still holds it was never reached.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the rooms as rows of numbers. Use -1 for a wall, 0 for a gate and 2147483647 for an empty room.

vars.meaning: number of cells in the grid (rows times columns)

compare.bruteLabel: Search from every room to find its nearest gate

rows.name: BFS from each empty room
rows.note: Every room runs its own search until it meets a gate. Most of the work repeats.

rows.name: BFS from all gates together
rows.note: Each room is reached once and written once. The grid copy and the queue are the extra memory.

fast.takeaway: Searching from the targets instead of from every room turns many searches into one. The first visit of a room is always the closest gate.

stages.title: Queue all gates
stages.note: Every gate goes into the queue. They all sit at distance 0, so they spread at the same speed.

stages.title: One ring per distance
stages.note: Each pass gives distance d to every INF neighbour of the current ring. Walls, gates and written rooms are skipped.

stages.title: Return the grid
stages.note: Rooms that were never reached still hold INF. They have no path to any gate.

edges.title: No gates
edges.why: The queue starts empty, so no ring is ever made. Every room stays INF.

edges.title: Room behind a wall
edges.why: The wall blocks the only path. The room is not reachable, so it keeps INF.

edges.title: Equal distance to two gates
edges.why: Both gates reach the middle room at the same ring. Either way the distance is 1.

edges.title: Empty grid
edges.why: No rows to scan. The queue is empty and the result is an empty grid.

gotchas.text: Use rooms.map(row => [...row]) to copy. A plain [...rooms] shares the row arrays, so the caller's grid would be overwritten as well.
Do not test cells for truthiness. A gate is 0, which is falsy, but a wall is -1, which is truthy. Compare with === INF so each of the three kinds of cell is treated on purpose.
int is 64-bit on most machines, so 2147483647 is safe. In int32 code, 2147483647 + 1 wraps to a negative number. Only ever compare against INF.
Test out[nb] === INF, not out[nb] > d. A gate (0) and a wall (-1) are both below INF, so they are skipped. A room already written has a smaller number, so it is skipped too.

recap.key: Queue every gate, spread ring by ring, and write the ring number on each INF room on first visit.
recap.complexity: Time O(rows x cols). Space O(rows x cols).
moves: Each ring: give distance d to INF neighbours
Skip walls, gates and written rooms
Rooms left at INF are unreachable
